history.notes: Initial release candidate: local Control4 feedback from one Philips Hue motion accessory over the on-bridge CLIP API v2 (HTTPS, developers.meethue.com). Clean-room original engineering; the pairing, transport, TLS posture, LAN guard, eventstream framing, and reconnect backoff are ported from the shipped IntegrateIT Hue Bridge driver rather than reinvented. · Scope stated in the manifest, the driver header, Start here, the trust section, and Print Configuration: this is a LIGHTING AND COMFORT driver, NOT a security, surveillance, or intrusion device, and not a listed alarm path. Philips Hue Developer Terms §8.2 forbid security/surveillance use of the Hue API, and a battery accessory on a consumer mesh cannot carry a life-safety decision. Never bind it into a security partition. · Link-button pairing built in: Pair (Link Button) POSTs `/api` with `generateclientkey`, handles the error-101 "press the button" round-trip, and stores the returned application key in the password-typed property — never printed, never logged (it rides only in the `hue-application-key` header). · Discover Sensors reads `GET /clip/v2/resource/device` and lists only devices whose service list contains a `motion` service, numbered; Bind Selected Sensor binds the chosen entry into the persisted `Sensor Device` property. Clear Binding and any rebind reset every reading to unknown and fire nothing — no observation has been made against the new id yet. · The bound sensor's four services (motion, light_level, temperature, device_power) are matched two independent ways — the resource names the bound device as its `owner`, or its id is one already learned on a resync — so another sensor's services, a light, a scene, or the SSE envelope's own event id can never move this instance's state. · Push feedback: consumes the /eventstream/clip/v2 SSE stream and publishes MOTION, CONTACT_STATE (OPENED / CLOSED / UNKNOWN, the verified Control4 contact vocabulary), MOTION_ENABLED, LIGHT_LEVEL, LIGHT_LEVEL_RAW, TEMPERATURE, BATTERY_LEVEL, BATTERY_STATE, LAST_MOTION (the bridge's own `creationtime`), STATE_STALE, and BRIDGE_ONLINE; fires Motion Detected/Cleared, Sensing Enabled/Disabled, Battery Low, Bridge Online/Offline, Event Stream Reconnected, and Sensor State Stale. SSE parsing tolerates arbitrary chunk boundaries and keep-alive comments. · Light level is converted honestly: CLIP reports `10000*log10(lux)+1`, the driver inverts it to `lux = 10 ^ ((light_level - 1) / 10000)` and publishes the raw value alongside so the conversion is auditable. A reported 0 sits below the formula's meaningful floor (inverting it yields 0.9998 lux), so the driver publishes 0 lux rather than round that up to 1. Both the flat CLIP fields and the newer `*_report` shapes are read for motion, light level, and temperature. Temperature converts C→F unless Temperature Units says otherwise, and is documented as an in-housing trend signal, not a thermostat reference. · Baseline silence where it belongs, and nowhere else. The first motion reading, the first enabled-flag reading, and the ONE catch-up read after a blind gap all adopt without firing a transition. What the eventstream delivers once it is back does fire: the driver sends no `If-None-Match`, so the bridge replays nothing and a frame arriving on a live stream is a change happening now — including the very first frame after a reconnect, which is usually the walk-past the dealer cares about. The gap token is one-shot and scoped to the motion feed, so a build running on the resync heartbeat alone resumes firing as soon as it has a good read, and a failed battery read never suppresses a motion transition the driver did watch. Battery Low is the deliberate exception in the other direction — a low battery is a standing condition, not a transition, so it reports the first time it is seen and latches until the level recovers. · Stream-loss honesty: a dropped eventstream — or a resync that gets no answer, which is the only signal a build without streaming has — publishes BRIDGE_ONLINE false, fires Bridge Offline and Sensor State Stale, raises STATE_STALE, and relabels Motion State `Stale (feed down) — last seen …`. The last observed values stay published because they are the last thing that was actually true — labelled, never frozen and presented as live, and never replaced by an invented zero. The documented trade is that a change during the blind gap moves the variables but fires no event. · One eventstream at a time. Connect runs on every relevant property change and on every rebind, so the driver refuses to stack a second long-lived transfer on a healthy one. A C4:url() transfer cannot be aborted, so a stream that has been deliberately replaced (Reconnect Event Stream, a rebind, a new bridge address) stays on the wire until the bridge closes it — it carries the generation it was opened under and is ignored from the moment it is replaced, so an abandoned transfer can neither re-apply state nor announce an outage over the stream that took over. Teardown retires the generation for the same reason: a socket closing a minute after OnDriverDestroyed cannot re-arm the reconnect timer. · Enable Sensing / Disable Sensing (PUT the motion service `enabled` flag) is the ONLY writable surface, and both re-check LicenseGate() at wire-write time. Neither fires Sensing Enabled/Disabled — the read-back does, which also means the events fire when someone flips the sensor in the Hue app. A write before any successful read refuses locally, by name, with the fix ("Motion service id unknown — run Resync Now first"). · LAN guard at the ONE transport chokepoint, ahead of header assembly, so the resync, the device read, the pairing claim, the eventstream, and the two writes are all covered — including the boot-time reads, which is the exact path a prior driver leaked an application key through. A blocked host produces zero requests of any kind; the runtime suite asserts the request count against the blocked address is 0 after boot and after every command and action. · Honest TLS trust model: the bridge is self-signed, so the driver connects over HTTPS with CA verification disabled and pins trust to the LAN address + application key; a broken TLS handshake fails closed and never downgrades to plaintext. A single bounded retry honors 429 Retry-After (no retry storm), and stream reconnects use bounded backoff (5s → 60s cap). · No bindable Control4 CONTACT_SENSOR connection, deliberately. Producer-side contact delivery — this driver pushing OPENED/CLOSED to a bound consumer — is unverified SDK surface (still fenced as unverified in the contact-relay template, and shipped by no IntegrateIT driver), and a binding that looks wired while delivering nothing is worse than no binding. Motion reaches Composer as variables and events instead, with CONTACT_STATE carrying the same vocabulary; the runtime suite pins this structurally by failing if a proxy or a CONTACT_SENSOR connection ever appears in the rendered driver.xml. · Known limits: one sensor per instance; sensitivity, outdoor daylight thresholds, and Hue-app automations are not exposed; light level is a conversion rather than a calibrated measurement; temperature reads warm because the sensor sits inside the housing; a change during a stream gap moves the variables but fires no event. · Verified against the Control4 API simulator only — `releaseStatus: release-candidate`, `hardwareStatus: simulation-verified`. Acceptance on a physical Hue Bridge, a physical motion accessory, and a physical controller is not attached to this release.
